title: A matrix is a map in coordinates
learningObjective: Interpret matrix columns and change of basis as representations of a linear map.

retrieve.bodyMarkdown: A map is determined by what it does to a basis. How can those images be recorded as numbers?

encounter.bodyMarkdown: The same vector can have coordinates $(4,2)$ or $(3,1)$, depending on the chosen basis. The vector has not moved; the description changed.

explain.bodyMarkdown: For input basis $B$ and output basis $C$, column $j$ of $[T]_{C\leftarrow B}$ is $[T(b_j)]_C$. Thus $[T(v)]_C=[T]_{C\leftarrow B}[v]_B$. If $P$ has a new basis as columns in old coordinates, then $[v]_{old}=P[v]_{new}$. For an operator represented by $A$ in the old basis, the new matrix is $P^{-1}AP$: convert in, apply the map, convert out. Matrix order matters; the rightmost operation acts first.

reflect.bodyMarkdown: Always state the ordered bases and direction of conversion. Changing coordinates does not change the map or its intrinsic rank.

hints.bodyMarkdown: Evaluate the matrix on a basis coordinate vector.
Matrix multiplication selects a column for a standard unit input.
The chosen column is the output coordinate list.
Multiplying by the $j$th standard coordinate vector selects column $j$. That input represents the $j$th input basis vector.

problems.solutionMarkdown: Multiplying by the $j$th standard coordinate vector selects column $j$. That input represents the $j$th input basis vector.

problems.promptMarkdown: In $B=((1,1),(1,-1))$, the vector $v$ has coordinates $(2,3)$. What is the second ordinary coordinate of $v$?

hints.bodyMarkdown: Convert basis coordinates back to an actual vector.
Use coordinates as coefficients of the ordered basis.
The second coordinate is $2-3$.
Reconstruct $v=2(1,1)+3(1,-1)=(5,-1)$. The requested coordinate is $-1$.

problems.promptMarkdown: If $[v]_{old}=P[v]_{new}$, the new matrix of an operator with old matrix $A$ is:

hints.bodyMarkdown: Follow an input through both coordinate systems.
Compositions act from right to left.
The last step converts old output coordinates back to new.
First apply $P$ to enter old coordinates, then $A$, then $P^{-1}$ to return. Reading these right to left gives $P^{-1}AP$.

problems.solutionMarkdown: First apply $P$ to enter old coordinates, then $A$, then $P^{-1}$ to return. Reading these right to left gives $P^{-1}AP$.

problems.promptMarkdown: Let $T(1,0)=(2,3)$ and $T(0,1)=(-1,4)$. Enter the two entries of the first column of its standard matrix.

hints.bodyMarkdown: Identify which input basis vector defines the first column.
Use the column interpretation of a linear map.
Only the first of the two given images is needed.
The first column is the image of the first standard basis vector, namely $(2,3)$. Images belong in columns, not rows.

problems.solutionMarkdown: The first column is the image of the first standard basis vector, namely $(2,3)$. Images belong in columns, not rows.
